- If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >95), model often overshoots downward; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 3–5 periods.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops from peak), model fails to adjust; force forecast to align with recent 5-day average.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.25), model may overreact; cap forecast growth at 1–2% above prior period unless sentiment >0.5.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the cycle; apply a “lag correction”: subtract 1–3% from forecast for first 5 days.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 3 days, reset forecast to 3-day moving average of true values for next 5 days.
